narrative.coaching_note: Clean your hands with alcohol rub after you touch the bedside surroundings and before you pick up your phone. You touched bed rail A starting at 1.6 seconds, and that contamination moved to your bare hand. You then touched call button and then touched phone starting at 12.4 seconds, so the phone became contaminated from your hand. You then touched resident A starting at 21.4 seconds without cleaning your hands right before that contact, so resident A was exposed. Use alcohol rub for the full 20 seconds at each of those times to break this chain and protect the next thing you touch. Cleaning your hands after the bedside contact would have kept your bare hand and gloved hand, phone, and resident A clean.
narrative.audit_summary: Bare-hand sequence from bed rail A (source) at 1.6 seconds led to transfer to call button at 7.6 seconds, to phone at 12.4 seconds, and to resident A at 21.4 seconds, with one resident exposure. No hand hygiene events occurred. Compliance was 0 of 2 opportunities overall, including Moment 1 at 0 of 1 and Moment 5 at 0 of 1; Moments 2 and 4 had no opportunities. Missed Moment 5 at 11 seconds preceded phone contamination, and missed Moment 1 at 21.4 seconds preceded resident A contact. No glove use issues were noted. Contamination remained on bare hand, gloved hand, bed rail A, call button, phone, and resident A. Disinfect bed rail A, call button, phone, and resident A's bedside zone (linen and surfaces) with an EPA List H registered disinfectant effective against MRSA.
narrative.top_fix: The highest-impact single change in this clip was hand hygiene at 11 seconds.
